title: Ethiopian Condiment Platter
community: Ethiopian celebration tables — all condiments assembled
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Condiment Platter — the complete set of Ethiopian table condiments assembled: Awaze (ETH144), Silsi (ETH146), Ayib with Herbs (ETH145), Honey Butter (ETH152), Timatim Selata (ETH147), Berbere Oil (ETH155), and Green Chilli Paste (ETH149). The full Ethiopian condiment experience.
longDesc: The Ethiopian condiment platter is brought to the celebration table alongside the mesob — each condiment providing a different flavour dimension: fierce heat (awaze, mitmita), fresh acid (silsi, timatim), cooling dairy (ayib), sweet richness (honey butter), and oil richness (berbere oil). Together they complete the Ethiopian flavour universe.
steps: Make berbere oil (ETH155) first — it needs time to infuse.
Make ayib with herbs (ETH145) — 2 hours for draining.
Arrange all in small ramekins on a wooden board.
chefTips: Awaze and berbere oil can be made days ahead.
Silsi and timatim salad must be made the day of.
Ayib needs 2 hours of draining — plan ahead.
Arrange by colour for maximum visual impact.
commonMistakes: Last-minute preparation of everything — most condiments improve with time.
sustainabilityTips: The condiment platter uses ingredients that are all locally sourced from Ethiopian producers.
healthBenefits: The complete condiment platter provides the full Ethiopian flavour spectrum — fierce heat to cooling dairy to sweet to acid. Together they ensure the entire meal is a complete sensory experience.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian condiment platter is the flavour toolkit of the great Ethiopian meal — every possible flavour dimension available at once. The Ethiopian tradition of placing multiple condiments on the table simultaneously reflects the philosophy of abundance: that the well-prepared host ensures that every guest can adjust the meal to their precise preference.
